summary.overview: Strong static-app discipline routes agent work well: AGENTS.md names owners and hard constraints, CI mechanically enforces them, and a fast unit suite exercises the LLM layer including recovery paths. The gaps are at the edges of that wiring: the highest-churn interview loop is verified only manually, the key-leak scan recognizes one key shape, and session records are too thin to judge repeated work or whether captured learning helped.

dimensions.label: Task Understanding
dimensions.summary: AGENTS.md routes decisions to PLAN.md and TASKS.md, states a per-task Definition of Done and six hard constraints, and the commit history shows task-scoped work with logged rationale; no session-linked episode proves day-to-day application.

dimensions.label: Controlled Execution
dimensions.summary: The documented pnpm command surface was exercised during review (test, typecheck, lint all pass), asset preparation is wired into dev/build, and BYOK keys stay in localStorage; host-side permission and deployment boundaries remain unobserved.

dimensions.label: Change Validation
dimensions.summary: Pure-logic layers have fast, focused tests including negative and recovery cases, and past fixes were diagnosed and revalidated with mutation checks; the highest-churn interview orchestration path has no automated check mapped to it, and the key-leak gate covers one pattern.

dimensions.label: Reliable Delivery
dimensions.summary: CI gates lint, typecheck, tests, build, static-export assertions, and a key scan, with Pages deploy chained on successful CI; no current-revision acceptance decision, deployment record, or rollback path could be opened from the repository.

dimensions.label: Learning Capture
dimensions.summary: A bounded review completed but session records admit no comparable episodes, so repeated work cannot be confirmed or ruled out and no captured learning has a later outcome to prove its effect.

findings.title: Interview loop changes rely on manual verification only
findings.reason: Fact: hooks/use-interview.ts and app/interview/interview-screen.tsx own the interview turn lifecycle (busy guard, abort, retry/skip, truncation buffer reset) and sit among the most-churned files in the 30-day history, yet no test file maps to them and vitest.config.ts includes only **/*.test.ts, so even a conventional hook test in .tsx form would not run. Inference: a real truncation-recovery fix already crossed this seam — the llm.ts side gained focused tests while the coordinated use-interview.ts change was verified manually, so a regression like a stuck busy state, double submit, or abort race has no automated detector. AGENTS.md testing guidance only mandates tests for pure logic, so this is an observed verification gap rather than a stated-rule violation. Owner: hooks/use-interview.ts plus the vitest include pattern. Uncertainty: the code shows defensive patterns (busyRef guard, finally-block cleanup), and the guidance may intentionally exclude this layer.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Add the smallest automated check that exercises the interview turn lifecycle in hooks/use-interview.ts. First discover how the existing vitest setup (node environment, include **/*.test.ts) can run a hook-level test; extend the include pattern only if that is the cheapest route, and keep the existing lib tests untouched. Cover at minimum: the busy guard rejecting a second submit while a turn is in flight, abort cleanup on unmount, and the truncation-retry buffer reset. Follow the testing guidance style in AGENTS.md (deterministic logic, mocked fetch).

## Validation

- Run pnpm typecheck and pnpm test; the new test executes under the existing CI command
- Temporarily break the busy guard and confirm the new test fails
- Confirm pnpm lint stays clean
expectedOutput: Update the existing Test owner identified by the reviewed evidence and retain a focused validation result.

findings.title: Non-standard API key shapes pass the CI leak scan
findings.reason: Fact: AGENTS.md hard constraint #2 says no API key may appear in the repo, bundle, env files, or CI, and .github/workflows/ci.yml enforces it by grepping the repo and build output; the inspected pattern matches only sk-<20+ alphanumerics>. Inference: keys with other shapes (provider prefixes such as sk-or-, xai-, or base64-style tokens) commit and deploy without tripping the gate, so the explicit constraint is only partially enforced. Owner: .github/workflows/ci.yml key-scan step. Uncertainty: the project declares no required pattern breadth, and BYOK keys live in user browsers, so this is defense-in-depth rather than an observed leak.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Broaden the key-leak scan in .github/workflows/ci.yml so it covers the key shapes the project actually supports, per the BYOK guidance in AGENTS.md and README (OpenAI-compatible endpoints such as OpenRouter, Groq, Ollama). Discover the current grep step first; add patterns for known provider prefixes and a long-token heuristic while keeping the scan limited to repo and build output so legitimate example text is not flagged.

## Validation

- Run the same grep locally against a throwaway fixture containing each supported key shape and confirm every shape matches
- Confirm the scan still passes on the clean repository and static build output
- Keep the workflow permissions and triggers unchanged

findings.title: Repeated work cannot be detected or turned into reusable improvements from current session records
findings.reason: Fact: the bounded 30-day review admitted only one short session with two unclosed candidate episodes and zero validation events; the evidence bundle flags source roots as missing-optional-root and disabled-source-root, and learning diagnostics report insufficient recurrence with no later outcome window. Inference: with no normalized task events, the project cannot decide whether repeated procedures exist worth making durable, or whether the captured project memories ever improved a later result — the learning boundary stays unresolved rather than clean. This is an evidence-gap finding, not a claim that no work happened. Owner: workspace session-evidence sources for this provider. Uncertainty: the emptiness may reflect disabled or unretained session sources rather than absent activity.
